correctness.rationale: Conjugation by u·σ is a half-turn about u, so the Bloch matrix is (λI+(1−λ)uu^T)R and preserves the norm of v=R^Tu. The exposed equality u^T Mv=1 forces C v=u for every contributing vertex C. If nonempty, these vertices form one coset of the rotations fixing v. The proper signed permutations with nontrivial fixed directions have axes through coordinate, face-diagonal or body-diagonal directions, with stabilizer orders 4, 2 and 3 respectively; all other directions have order 1. This follows by listing rotation types of signed permutations, including quarter-turns and half-turns on coordinate axes, half-turns on edge (face-diagonal) axes, and third-turns on body diagonals. Multiplying by C_0^T leaves the axis scalar one and transverse multiplication by λ exp(iδ). Every allowed Clifford transverse block is multiplication by an h-th root of unity, so matching the two real entries is exactly the polygon test. Choice of representative rotates the polygon and choice of transverse basis preserves the coefficient. For 0<p<1, including p=1/2, h=1 is excluded by |z|<1. At fixed third coordinate each possible nonvertical azimuth for a given special axis orbit differs by a multiple of π/2; a non-Clifford R_z therefore cannot connect v to u within an orbit unless u is vertical. The diamond gives the aligned inequality. For p=1 one can take u=(cos(θ/2),sin(θ/2),0), for which the equatorial half-turn followed in composition order after R_z(θ) gives the x-axis Clifford half-turn. The real-axis slice of the body-diagonal triangle is [−1/2,1], giving p<=3/4; the segment and diamond contain [−1,1]. The packaged LP checker and listed cases were inspected but not executed; no numerical tolerance proves the criterion.
residual_risks: The criterion is for exact mixtures of unitary one-qubit Clifford channels for the stated post-unitary noise model; it does not address instrumental, approximate or nonunitary decompositions.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The facet theorem can decide every specific instance and occupies the general membership claim. The present reduction evaluates this structured slice by stabilizer order and gives a uniform obstruction in the phase-gate subfamily, rather than treating a fresh instance of the ambient facet test as novelty.

evidence: Rigidity plus the old vertex set supplies the exposed convex hull. Identifying it with the single coset and evaluating the transverse action gives the four small polygons; the special-axis orbit at fixed third coordinate then yields exact exclusion even at λ=0.
The body-diagonal real-axis interval comes from the evaluated triangular section, rather than a parameter change from the prior aligned square.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The coset reduction is elementary once pure-direction rigidity is available and does not constitute a new general face theory. The exact slice and universal tilted exclusion require the stabilizer/orbit analysis and are not provided by substituting the channel into the old aligned threshold or observing finite numerical cases.

originality.rationale: The ambient Clifford polytope, pure-direction rigidity and circle-moment reduction, aligned dephasing threshold and documented p=1 tilted exception have prior coverage. The supported distinct claim is the evaluated cyclic polygon classification for arbitrary rotation and axis, with the resulting strict analytical exclusion for arbitrary non-Clifford phase angle throughout the intermediate-p interval and the body-diagonal threshold. It is not a new general membership formulation or the first identification of those aligned and endpoint cases.
residual_risks: An equivalent stabilizer-face classification in differently indexed Clifford-polytope literature could overlap. The comparison is bounded and establishes no global priority.

value.rationale: The exact slice classification replaces an ambient membership computation with at most a four-vertex polygon and gives constructive weights when feasible. For tilted dephasing it resolves the qualitative question of zero non-Clifford unitary cost at intermediate noise without relying on a numerical scan and separates a real endpoint exception. That is useful beyond restating the known ambient linear program or aligned threshold.
residual_risks: No general result about positive optimal unraveling cost or multi-qubit simulation and fault tolerance is established.
